recap.text: Porthus crawled in the fifteenth season as a High Elf rogue. He wrote the second edition of a cookbook that is handed down. Now called Dr. Hu, he spends a small NFC's money on the crawler who holds his book. Production does not know how to bill him.

Doctor Hu predicted the crawler would talk the AI into turning off safety protections and how the council would respond. He finds the crew of the converted Long Haul garbage freighter, renamed Homecoming Queen, and promises them death. Fifty thousand former crawlers hide inside, cleared by the AI for on-boarding as troopers for Carl and Donut.

Porthus sits in a zero zone with one shaking arm and declines fifteen seasons as low-floor undead to take game guide for one hundred seasons. As Doctor Hu, he runs the Crawler Project and the Open Intellect Pacifist Network. He refurbishes a garbage freighter into a passenger liner, but the group scatters when accused of being a terrorist organization. Porthus uses an embedded agent to change Volteeg's code so the former pet avoids the Bone Clan.

beats.headline: The second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject crawled in the fifteenth season, chose the High Elf race and a rogue’s class, and wrote the second edition of the book that keeps being handed down. He now goes by Dr. Hu, and he is spending a small NFC's money, more of it than anyone should ask about, on the crawler who holds his book. He is therefore both an advertisement for the dungeon and a witness against it, and production has never worked out how to bill him.
beats.gist: Porthus crawled in the fifteenth season as a High Elf rogue and wrote a cookbook.

beats.headline: Two promises from Doctor Hu
beats.text: Doctor Hu predicted all of it: that the crawler would talk the AI into turning off the safety protections, and how the council would respond. He sought out the crew of a converted Long Haul garbage freighter, now renamed Homecoming Queen, and told them first that he could promise only two things, and the first was eventual death. Hidden inside it are fifty thousand former crawlers, cleared by the AI for on-boarding as troopers for Carl and Donut's team.
beats.gist: Doctor Hu predicts the AI safety protections will turn off and tells the Homecoming Queen crew.

beats.headline: He picks game guide
beats.text: Subject sits in a zero zone at the start of the eleventh floor, still bloody, one arm shaking, facing an attorney who has brought snacks. His party was twenty strong at the end of the ninth. As far as he knows he is the last of it: he ran when she begged him to, and left behind a friend whose foot was stuck. He declines fifteen seasons as low-floor undead and thirty as a city attendant, and takes game guide, one hundred seasons. He survived the indentureship. Current status: missing, and wanted by Syndicate Security.
beats.gist: Porthus survives an indentureship as a game guide and is wanted by Syndicate Security.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, per Tipid
beats.text: Tipid supplies more of the file. Subject, as Doctor Hu, runs the Crawler Project, an NFC for former crawlers, whose campaigning made every newly released crawler a Syndicate citizen with free healthcare and guaranteed housing. He also formed the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, a smaller group aimed at ending the crawl altogether. It was his idea to refurbish a garbage freighter into a passenger liner and call for former crawlers to come back in. When they were accused of being a terrorist organization, they scattered. Tipid does not know where he is.
beats.gist: Tipid provides a file on Doctor Hu, who runs the Crawler Project and the Open Intellect Pacifist Network.

beats.headline: It is not too late
beats.text: Porthus's work, done quietly: someone working for the Pacifist Network, embedded deep in the Syndicate bureaucracy changed the code on Volteeg's designation, so a former pet passed for a former indentured refugee rather than a former crawler, and was not dragged off to the Bone Clan with the others. The help was meant to be untraceable, or the few former crawlers among the mercenaries would be purged. Porthus underestimated the warlords: those crawlers were dead already, and King Rust had jumped several levels. It was Rosetta who recognised Volteeg's name. It's not too late to do something about it, Porthus told him.
beats.gist: Porthus tells him it is not too late to do something about Volteeg.

relations.note: Publicly disowned, privately in close contact
